ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
An insulated track ABC is placed in a vertical plane. The AB section is a smooth semicircular track with a radius of $R = 0.40 \mathrm{m}$. The BC section is a rough horizontal track. A bounded uniform electric field of $E = 1.0 \times 10^3 \mathrm{V/m}$ directed horizontally to the right is distributed within the vertical plane where the BC track is located, with AB being the left boundary of the electric field. A slider (treated as a point mass) with a mass of $m = 0.04 \mathrm{kg}$ and a charge of $q = -1 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{C}$ is released from rest at a certain point on BC. The normal force exerted by the track on the slider at point A is exactly zero. Given that the coefficient of kinetic friction between the slider and BC is $\mu = 0.05$ and $g$ is taken as $10 \mathrm{m/s}^2$.

1. What is the magnitude of the velocity $v_A$ of the slider when it passes through point A?
2. What is the distance $x$ from the release point of the slider on the BC track to point B?
3. What is the minimum speed $v$ of the slider during its motion in the air after leaving point A?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, AB can be seen as a vertical dashed-line diameter, with A at the upper end, B at the lower end, and O at the midpoint of AB; on the left side of AB is a section of smooth semicircular track. Point B is connected to the right to the horizontal track BC, and there is a schematic of a small slider on BC. In the region on the right side of AB, multiple horizontal rightward electric field lines are drawn, labeled E, indicating that the direction of the electric field is to the right, and AB is the left boundary of the electric field. Reasoning: At point A, the center of the circle O is below A, and the supporting force of the track on the slider N_A=0, so only gravity provides the centripetal force: mg = m v_A^2/R, so v_A = sqrt(gR)=sqrt(10×0.40)=2 m/s. From B to A, the semicircular track is smooth, and according to the problem statement/figure AB is the boundary of the electric field; take this section as having no friction and do not count the work done by the electric field; A is higher than B by 2R. The mechanical energy relation is K_B = K_A + mg(2R). Substituting K_A = 1/2 m v_A^2 = 1/2×0.04×4 = 0.08 J, mg(2R)=0.04×10×0.80=0.32 J, gives K_B=0.40 J. From the release point to B, the slider moves leftward on the rough horizontal BC. The electric field is to the right and q<0, so the electric field force is to the left, with magnitude |q|E=1×10^-4×1.0×10^3=0.10 N; the friction force is to the right, with magnitude μmg=0.05×0.04×10=0.02 N. The work done by the resultant external force is (|q|E-μmg)x=K_B, that is, (0.10-0.02)x=0.40, solving gives x=5 m. After leaving A, the initial velocity is horizontally to the right, with magnitude v_A=2 m/s; the electric field force is to the left, acceleration a_x=-|q|E/m=-0.10/0.04=-2.5 m/s^2, and in the vertical direction a_y=-g=-10 m/s^2. Therefore v_x=2-2.5t, v_y=-10t. The square of the speed v^2=(2-2.5t)^2+(10t)^2=4-10t+106.25t^2. This quadratic reaches its minimum value at t=10/(2×106.25), v_min^2=4-100/(4×106.25)=3.7647, so v_min≈1.94 m/s.
